title: On-call rotation heatmap + probabilistic responder suggester with safe opt-in
author: Oscar Vega
release_notes: Adds on-call rotation heatmap and a privacy-preserving probabilistic responder suggester; opt-in config and rollout notes included; backwards-compatible and disabled by default.
description: This PR introduces a visual on-call rotation heatmap and a probabilistic responder suggestion service designed to help first responders pick the best on-call contacts during high-noise incidents. Motivation: paging fatigue and brittle static routing cause delays during cross-team incidents; operators want quick, confidence-scored suggestions with an audit trail and opt-out controls. Key features: 1) Heatmap generator: background worker that aggregates recent alert ownership, response latency, and effective resolution rate into a daily/weekly heatmap tile set stored in blobstore for fast retrieval; 2) Probabilistic responder suggester: lightweight model that combines structured signals (recent responder activity, escalation paths, time-of-day, timezone, rotation schedule) and fuzzy signals (inferred domain affinity from recent incident tags) to return a ranked list of suggested responders with calibrated confidence scores; 3) Safety & privacy: suggestions are gated behind an org-level opt-in flag and a per-team affinity threshold; low-confidence responses are suppressed and surface a "suggest colleagues" fallback; audit log entries are emitted for every suggestion; 4) UX surface: new /oncall/heatmap REST endpoint and a compact heatmap widget for the Slack triage flow; the triage slack modal now shows top-3 suggested responders and a short autogenerated runbook snippet; 5) Observability: new metrics (ib.suggester.requests, ib.suggester.confidence_bucket, ib.heatmap.generation_latency) and dashboards plus two alert rules for model drift and heatmap job lag; 6) Migration & rollout: feature flag gated, rollout plan to 10% orgs for 2 weeks then 50% with monitoring gates, and clear revert steps. Checklist: - [x] Background aggregator and heatmap tile format implemented; - [x] Suggester service and k8s deployment chart; - [x] Slack modal + heatmap widget workendpoints; - [x] Metrics, dashboards, and alerts; - [x] Privacy opt-in and audit logging; - [x] Unit and integration tests; Known limitations: suggestion model uses a small heuristics-backed logistic ranking (no PII model training); heatmap resolution is per-team only (no user-level heatmaps); suggestion latency target is 120ms under normal load but may spike during heavy incidents and is throttled. Related work: follows on from ENG-1429 incident attribution and ENG-1598 runbook templating. Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/notes/oncall-heatmap-design and runbook templates https://internal.redwood.example/runbooks/triage.
